rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing the simplest configuration: RNA-only with singleprofile, PCA_n2000 encoder, no image data, and no aggregation/fusion. This clarifies the performance of the minimal viable model, isolating the effect of RNA encoding and profile setting. It provides a reference point for comparing more complex configurations later.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only single-profile models with PCA encoding achieve 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of multi-profile settings with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile structure while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder consistent. It balances exploration of profile settings with minimal additional complexity, providing critical insight into whether multi-profile configurations improve performance without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) in the multiprofile setup with avgpool aggregation improves performance. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, while maintaining consistent aggregation and profile settings. This balances exploitation of the multiprofile advantage with exploration of encoder improvements.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile and scvi_n200 RNA encoder significantly improve performance (config_005: 0.650 accuracy). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (a more complex method) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation strategy. It balances exploitation of known effective components (scvi_n200, multiprofile) with exploration of a critical design choice (aggregation method).

Existing evidence shows that for RNA-only models, multiprofile setups with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and avgpool aggregation achieve higher accuracy (0.650) than pca_n2000. This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (a new representation) in the same multiprofile setup with avgpool aggregation isolates the impact of the RNA encoder. This clarifies whether scgpt outperforms scvi_n200, a critical design choice with sparse prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only with multiprofile and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_006) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (a different model) with transformer aggregation (which slightly outperformed avgpool in config_006) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while leveraging the potentially beneficial aggregation method, balancing exploration of critical design choices with building on prior promising directions.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 encoder, and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests whether adding image data (resnet50) with multimodal fusion (concat) can further improve performance, clarifying the impact of multimodal integration. It directly builds on the best-performing RNA encoder and aggregation method, balancing exploitation of known strengths with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests whether combining this strong RNA encoder with image data (resnet50) using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could improve performance. It isolates the impact of multimodal fusion strategies while building on a proven RNA encoder and aggregation method, balancing exploitation of known strengths with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve high validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether using avgpool aggregation instead of transformer aggregation (while keeping other parameters the same) affects performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, which is critical for understanding model design trade-offs. This is a logical extension of the promising multimodal direction and helps resolve uncertainty about aggregation's impact.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA and resnet50 image encoders (e.g., config_033) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping other parameters consistent) impacts performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best next step as it directly addresses a key design choice (fusion) with minimal changes, leveraging prior success while exploring critical variations.
